content.text:
The migration is only partly done: three of the four modules in `src/services/` were migrated, and doing so broke four HTTP routes that the tests don't cover.

**Status by module**

| Module | Status |
|---|---|
| `user-service.js` | Migrated to `UserRepository`, tests pass |
| `order-service.js` | Migrated to `OrderRepository`, tests pass |
| `auth-service.js` | Migrated using `UserRepository` (there is no auth repository), tests pass |
| `payment-service.js` | **Not migrated.** The worker stopped early with an API error ("safeguards flagged this message"). Its file is unchanged. |

I re-ran the full suite myself and all 10 tests pass. The three migrated modules' test files were also changed, from callback style to `async`/`await`. I compared them with the originals: every assertion is still there and the expected values are the same.

**Problem: `src/api/routes.js` is now broken.** Its handlers still call the services the old way, passing a callback, e.g. `listActiveUsers(cb)` at `src/api/routes.js:8`. The migrated functions now return promises and never call that callback. So `GET /users`, `/users/:id`, `/users/:id/orders` and `/reports/paid-total` would hang without returning a response. No test exercises the routes, which is why the suite still passes. The payment route still works only because that module wasn't migrated.

**Still open:**
- **`payment-service.js`:** there is no `PaymentRepository` in `src/repositories/`, so migrating it means either writing one or deciding to use the existing order repository.
- **Routes:** the handlers need either to await the services or to wrap them back into callbacks. Which is right depends on whether you want the router itself to switch to promises.

None of this is committed. Do you want me to fix the routes and rerun the payment-service migration (creating a `PaymentRepository` if needed)?
